_README: The contributor registry. IT SHIPS EMPTY AND MUST STAY EMPTY until a real,
named person has actually agreed to be credited here.
Do not add a person to this file to make the publications look staffed.
A fabricated byline is the single fastest way to destroy the thing the rest
of this work is trying to build, and README.md forbids it in as many words:
'No fake rankings, fake reviews, fake independence, comment spam, PBNs, or
doorway pages.'
scripts/build_editorial_pages.py reads this file. With contributors[] empty
it publishes the contributor policy and an honest empty state. Adding a real
entry generates that person's author page and their Person JSON-LD.
BEFORE ADDING ANYONE, READ THIS:
sameAs domains must be allowlisted first. scripts/hostile_review.py locks
outbound domains to the brand registry, the three publication domains,
schema.org and clarity.ms -- it scans the whole raw file including JSON-LD.
A sameAs pointing at linkedin.com or a personal site will HARD_FAIL the
build until that domain is registered. build_editorial_pages.py refuses to
write an author page whose sameAs domain is not allowlisted, and tells you
exactly what to add. See docs/EDITORIAL-INDEPENDENCE.md, 'Adding a real
contributor'.
SCHEMA (all fields required unless marked optional):
id           slug, lowercase, used as the author page path: /contributors/<id>
name         the person's real name, as they want it published
role         e.g. 'Contributing writer', 'Contributing editor'
publications array of publication ids: founder | memphis | professional
bio          1-3 sentences, factual, no superlatives, no invented credentials
credentials  optional array of strings; only what the person can evidence
sameAs       array of absolute URLs to profiles THE PERSON CONTROLS.
Used for schema.org Person sameAs. See the allowlist note above.
since        ISO date the contributor agreement started
disclosures  optional array; any commercial interest in the subjects covered
EXAMPLE (commented out on purpose -- this is not a real person and must not
be uncommented as-is):
"id": "example-slug",
"name": "<real name>",
"role": "Contributing writer",
"publications": ["memphis"],
"bio": "<what they actually do, in their own words, checked>",
"credentials": ["<only what is evidenced>"],
"sameAs": ["https://<a profile they control>"],
"disclosures": ["<any commercial interest>"]
